extracted_factors.Label: Corporate Zero-Deforestation Commitments (ZDCs)
extracted_factors.Description: Commitments made by companies to not purchase products sourced from land cleared of forests. These commitments aim to halt deforestation and include environmental and social targets.

extracted_factors.Label: Traceability
extracted_factors.Description: The ability to track the origin of palm oil in the supply chain to ensure compliance with zero-deforestation commitments.

extracted_factors.Label: Smallholder Inclusion
extracted_factors.Description: Efforts to incorporate smallholder farmers into zero-deforestation initiatives, addressing their socio-economic needs and preventing exclusion.

extracted_factors.Label: Spatial and Functional Fit
extracted_factors.Description: The alignment between the geographic scope of zero-deforestation commitments and the actual ecological and social contexts they affect.

extracted_factors.Label: EU Deforestation Regulation
extracted_factors.Description: Regulatory framework by the European Union requiring due diligence in the supply chains of forest-risk commodities.

extracted_factors.Label: Deforestation Risk
extracted_factors.Description: The likelihood of forests being cleared for agricultural expansion, primarily driven by commodity demands like palm oil.

extracted_pain_points.description: Many companies struggle with achieving full traceability in their supply chains, especially to the plantation level.
Efforts to include smallholder farmers are insufficient, leading to potential exclusion from international markets.
High-quality ZDCs often do not align with areas needing protection due to differences in risk levels and forest vulnerability.
Lack of programs for supporting high-risk mills to comply with zero-deforestation commitments.
